about: Torqwave against the products that are real alternatives for what it does. Definitions live here; the cells for each Torqwave release live in snapshots/<version>.json.

values.yes: Built into the product at the edition assessed, and documented.
values.partial: A limited form; the note says how.
values.no: The product's own documentation shows it absent, or its scope excludes it and its documentation has no mention.
values.not confirmed: No first-party page was found that settles it. Counted as neither yes nor no.
values.info: A fact, not a yes or no (price, licence, dates). Never counted.

method: Every competitor cell was read from the product's own documentation, manual, feature or pricing page on the date in its snapshot, and keeps the page's address and a short quotation or a note of what was checked. Where no first-party page settled a cell it says 'not confirmed'.
Torqwave's cells come from this repository's README, guide, roadmap and changelog at the commit the snapshot names.
Only what ships in the product counts. Third-party plug-ins do not, and neither do separate downloads unless the note says so (those are 'partial').
Each product is assessed at the edition its snapshot names, usually the largest, so a cheaper edition may have less than its column shows.

Coverage of an area is a count: how many of the area's rows are yes, and how many partial. Rows are not weighted, and no single score or rank is computed across areas, because any weighting would be arbitrary.

The rows were chosen for what Torqwave aims at (sound design, writing music, work to picture, game audio), so they favour a product that is both an editor and a DAW. A product built for one job covers few rows outside it by design, which says nothing about how well it does that job.

A yes says a feature exists. It says nothing of its depth, its quality or how long it has been in use. Torqwave's features are new and mostly tested by its own suite, not by years of users; the 'maturity' facts under the matrix are there to keep that in view.

rows.title: Edits a single audio file
rows.definition: A destructive, sample-level editor for one audio file: open it, cut and paste, save it back.

rows.title: Spectrogram view
rows.definition: A spectrogram display of a file or clip.

rows.title: Spectral selection and editing
rows.definition: Selecting and editing a region in time and frequency (box, lasso or brush) in the spectrogram.

rows.title: Spectral heal
rows.definition: Removing a sound in the spectrogram by filling from its surroundings.

rows.title: Batch processing
rows.definition: Putting many files through the same steps unattended.

rows.title: Noise reduction
rows.definition: Broadband noise reduction built in.

rows.title: Click, hum and clipping repair
rows.definition: Click or pop removal, hum removal and clipped-peak repair, all built in; partial if only one or two.

rows.title: Reverb reduction
rows.definition: Reverb reduction built in.

rows.title: Dialogue isolation
rows.definition: Separating speech from background noise, built in.

rows.title: Stem separation
rows.definition: Splitting a music mix into stems (vocals, drums, bass, other), built in.

rows.title: Loudness (LUFS) measure and match
rows.definition: Measuring integrated loudness (EBU R128 / ITU-R BS.1770) and matching a LUFS target, built in.

rows.title: True-peak limiting or metering
rows.definition: A true-peak limiter or true-peak meter built in.

rows.title: Delivery-spec check with a report
rows.definition: Checking or conforming a file against a named delivery spec (EBU R128, ATSC A/85, streaming targets) with a report.

rows.title: Spectrum analyzer and phase meter
rows.definition: A spectrum analyzer and a stereo phase or correlation meter built in; partial if only one.

rows.title: Pitch correction
rows.definition: Pitch correction of a voice or solo line built in, automatic or by dragging notes.

rows.title: Multitrack sessions
rows.definition: Non-destructive multitrack sessions with audio clips on tracks.

rows.title: Buses and sends
rows.definition: Buses and sends in a mixer.

rows.title: Automation
rows.definition: Automation of volume, pan and effect or plug-in parameters.

rows.title: Takes and comping
rows.definition: Recording takes and comping between them.

rows.title: Audio follows the tempo
rows.definition: Audio clips that stretch to follow the project tempo.

rows.title: Surround mixing (5.1 or more)
rows.definition: 5.1 or 7.1 surround mixing; yes also when the product mixes Dolby Atmos.

rows.title: Dolby Atmos mixing
rows.definition: Dolby Atmos (object-based) mixing built in.

rows.title: Clip or scene launching
rows.definition: A grid for launching clips, patterns or scenes live.

rows.title: ARA 2 plug-ins
rows.definition: ARA 2 plug-in support.

rows.title: Piano roll and MIDI recording
rows.definition: MIDI note clips with a piano roll and MIDI recording.

rows.title: Step or drum grid
rows.definition: A step sequencer or drum grid for patterns.

rows.title: Factory MIDI patterns
rows.definition: Factory MIDI patterns, sequences or clips shipped with the product; the number when a first-party page states one.

rows.title: MIDI out and control surfaces
rows.definition: MIDI output to hardware, and control-surface or MIDI-learn support.

rows.title: Audio to MIDI
rows.definition: Converting audio to MIDI notes, built in.

rows.title: Notation editor
rows.definition: A score or notation editor.

rows.title: Built-in synthesizer
rows.definition: At least one built-in synthesizer instrument.

rows.title: Wavetable from your own audio
rows.definition: A built-in wavetable synth that makes a wavetable from the user's own audio.

rows.title: Built-in drum instrument
rows.definition: A built-in drum machine or drum sampler instrument.

rows.title: Built-in sampler
rows.definition: A built-in sampler instrument that plays the user's samples across the keys.

rows.title: Factory instrument sounds
rows.definition: Built-in instruments with factory presets; numbers only where a first-party page states them.

rows.title: Synth patch from a recording
rows.definition: Building an editable synth patch that imitates a recording (resynthesis or sound matching), built in.

rows.title: VST3
rows.definition: Hosts VST3 plug-ins.

rows.title: Audio Units (Mac)
rows.definition: Hosts Audio Units on macOS.

rows.title: LV2
rows.definition: Hosts LV2 plug-ins.

rows.title: CLAP
rows.definition: Hosts CLAP plug-ins.

rows.title: VST2
rows.definition: Hosts VST2 plug-ins.

rows.title: Video playback in sync
rows.definition: Plays a video in sync with the audio timeline.

rows.title: Sound written back into video
rows.definition: Writes the edited sound or the mix into a video file.

rows.title: SMPTE timecode
rows.definition: SMPTE timecode display.

rows.title: Scene-cut detection
rows.definition: Detects scene cuts in the video.

rows.title: Searchable sound library
rows.definition: A built-in searchable database or browser for the user's own sound-effects or sample collection, with tags or metadata search.

rows.title: A typed request becomes edits
rows.definition: An assistant that turns a typed request into edits or actions in the product.

rows.title: Machine learning runs locally
rows.definition: The product's machine-learning features run on the user's computer or network, not a cloud service; partial if some are cloud; no if all are cloud or there are none.

rows.title: Uses a model server you choose
rows.definition: Lets the user point AI features at a model server of their own choice.

rows.title: macOS
rows.definition: Officially supported on macOS.

rows.title: Windows
rows.definition: Officially supported on Windows.

rows.title: Linux
rows.definition: Officially supported on Linux.

rows.title: Open source
rows.definition: Source code published under an open-source licence.

info_rows.title: Price
info_rows.definition: Current list price from the vendor's own page, with currency, subscription or perpetual, and the date looked up.

info_rows.title: Licence model
info_rows.definition: Free, perpetual, subscription or mixed, and upgrade terms.

info_rows.title: First public release
info_rows.definition: The year of the product's first public release.

info_rows.title: Version assessed
info_rows.definition: The version assessed and its release date.

info_rows.title: Signed or notarized installers
info_rows.definition: Installers are code-signed or notarized, where a first-party page says so.

info_rows.title: Scripting or extension API
info_rows.definition: A documented scripting or extension API.

info_rows.title: Manual and interface languages
info_rows.definition: Languages of the official manual or interface, where a first-party page lists them.

products.name: Torqwave
products.why: The product this set tracks. The current column is the release the snapshot is made for.

products.name: Torqwave (previous release)
products.why: The release before, as its own column, so each release's gains show.

products.name: Adobe Audition
products.why: The commercial reference for a waveform and spectral editor with a multitrack; named in the brief, and Torqwave ships an Audition-style key set.

products.name: Audacity
products.why: The free, open-source editor most people try first; named in the brief, and the README offers Torqwave as an alternative to it.

products.name: iZotope RX
products.why: The reference for spectral repair and restoration, the job of Torqwave's repair suite.

products.name: Steinberg SpectraLayers
products.why: The reference for spectral editing by layers and for unmixing.

products.name: Steinberg WaveLab
products.why: The reference for mastering, loudness and delivery, the job of Torqwave's mastering suite.

products.name: FL Studio
products.why: Named in the brief; pattern-based writing with many built-in instruments, the area 0.20.0 moves into.

products.name: REAPER
products.why: A low-cost DAW on all three systems, widely used for sound design and game audio.

products.name: Ableton Live
products.why: The reference for clip launching and electronic music, the ground the Idea Board and the built-in instruments move into.

products.name: Bitwig Studio
products.why: A DAW on all three systems, Linux included, with a large set of built-in instruments.

products.name: Ardour
products.why: The open-source DAW: the other free-software route to multitrack work on Linux, macOS and Windows.

left_out.name: ocenaudio
left_out.why: A free editor for quick edits; without spectral editing or a multitrack it overlaps the Audacity column and adds no row where it differs.

left_out.name: Sound Forge
left_out.why: Windows only in its current Pro edition; WaveLab covers the mastering-editor place on more systems.

left_out.name: Logic Pro, Cubase/Nuendo, Pro Tools, Studio One
left_out.why: Each would add a column much like Live's or REAPER's; Logic is Mac only. Add one when a release moves into its ground (Nuendo or Pro Tools for picture work).
